Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.23% to 25,045 but decliners led 1,533 to 1,026
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.03% weighted by turnover, against -0.45% for the median stock, a gap of 2.5 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED rose 20.0% on 176 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “TRANSWORLD SHIPPING LINES LIMITED has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026.”.

Repco Home Finance Limited rose 11.9% on 93 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

Gujarat Natural Resources Limited rose 6.7% on 173 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Top PSU stock to buy: Brokerage sees 50% upside! Gujarat Energy shares gain 2% as profit surges 26% - Check target price”.

Aarti Drugs Limited rose 11.1% on 160 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Aarti Drugs shares defy weak market sentiment; skyrocket 11% today | Here's why; stock returns, performance”.

What happened
Breaking
Dollar sellers hit pause for US inflation data
The US Dollar Index paused its recent decline as traders positioned ahead of the upcoming US consumer price index report. Higher US inflation would push Treasury yields up, strengthening the dollar and weakening the Indian rupee. This mechanism threatens Foreign Portfolio Investor flows into Indian equities and raises import costs for domestic crude buyers. A CPI print above consensus would confirm capital outflows.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Buy Mphasis: target of Rs 3020: ICICI Securities
ICICI Securities issued a buy rating on Mphasis with a target price of 3,020 rupees. The target relies on anticipated revenue recovery in the US banking and financial services vertical, which generates over half of company revenue. Sustained earnings growth requires higher discretionary IT spending by American banks, which upcoming direct-channel TCV contract wins will confirm.
Moneycontrol
Gold dips ahead of US inflation data
Spot gold prices declined in early Asian trade ahead of US inflation data. Lower bullion prices reduce India's merchandise import bill, easing current account deficit pressures. For listed gold-loan non-banking financial companies like Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance, falling gold prices compress collateral valuation buffers and slow loan book expansion. US rate expectations will confirm price trends.
ET Markets · +1 other
Connected to your data
Top PSU stock to buy: Brokerage sees 50% upside! Gujarat Energy shares gain 2% as profit surges 26% - Check target price
Gujarat State Petronet reported a 21.9 percent year-on-year increase in second-quarter net profit to 639.27 crore rupees. The earnings performance was driven by higher gas transmission volumes and lower spot LNG input costs, which expanded operating margins. Tariff revision orders from the petroleum regulator will determine whether revenue growth persists in subsequent quarters.
Mint Markets
Aarti Drugs shares defy weak market sentiment; skyrocket 11% today | Here's why; stock returns, performance
Aarti Drugs rose 11 percent to an intraday high of 513 rupees on elevated trading volume. The price movement follows operational recovery in the active pharmaceutical ingredients segment, driven by lower key starting material costs imported from China. Second-quarter gross margin figures will confirm whether raw material input cost reductions translate into durable earnings growth.
Mint Markets
Your themes
Wall St jumps as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumps
Brent crude slipped below key support levels, easing US inflation expectations and lifting broader equities despite a selloff in Nvidia. For India, cheaper crude directly lowers the import bill, easing current account pressure and supporting the rupee. Lower input costs benefit margin-constrained domestic sectors like paints, lubricants, and chemicals, while reducing the risk of rate-hike spillovers from global central banks.
AI & data centresReuters Business · +1 other
Nvidia chips, Alibaba ties and Jensen Huang scandal: Inside Alice Huang's $100 million-plus pitch
This media report on a private venture pitch carries no fundamental implications for Indian listed equities.
AI & data centresMint Companies
NSE deploys liquid cooling for AI infra, plans over 80 GPUs this quarter
The National Stock Exchange is expanding its AI computing capacity to 80 GPUs this quarter, targeting 224, alongside liquid cooling deployment in its co-location center. This highlights rising domestic data center infrastructure intensity and cooling requirements. The shift benefits listed server builders like Netweb Technologies and data center cooling and electrical equipment suppliers such as Schneider Electric Infrastructure.
AI & data centresBS Markets
Govt may extend support measures in FY28 Budget to boost manufacturing of 100 products: Official
The government is preparing Budget FY28 incentives targeting 100 imported products across auto components, specialty chemicals, and heavy machinery. If implemented, production-linked concessions or duty protection will improve domestic market share and capital expenditure returns for auto ancillary firms like Bharat Forge and chemical manufacturers like Atul. Final product lists released by DPIIT will confirm sector-specific allocation sizes.
Import substitutionET Economy
Capital markets
Google unveils new AI chip variants as cloud demand surges
Google launched updated custom AI chips to capture rising cloud workload demand across enterprise clients. Proprietary chip adoption by hyperscalers lowers unit computing costs, driving enterprise cloud migration volumes. This expanded infrastructure spend supports order pipelines for Indian IT services providers handling cloud integration, software optimization, and custom silicon engineering services for global technology clients.
Reuters Business
Trump says Qatar, Saudi prefer peace in Iran conflict
US President Donald Trump stated that Saudi Arabia and Qatar prefer a peaceful outcome in regional tensions with Iran. De-escalation reduces crude oil risk premiums, lowering India's import bill and strengthening the rupee. Lower crude prices support gross margins for oil marketing companies like BPCL and paints maker Asian Paints. Weekly Brent crude settlement figures will confirm whether this geopolitical discount holds.
Reuters Business
Pentagon chief Hegseth expected to face House impeachment vote this week
This domestic US legislative matter has no financial mechanism reaching Indian equities.
Reuters Business
UK's Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in jail for rape, sexual assault
This criminal conviction has no direct or indirect impact on Indian equities or financial markets.
Reuters Business
Macro and economy
India's investment outlook strengthens as credit, exports rebound; inflation relief likely: HSBC
HSBC reported a surge in commercial credit and export recovery, alongside expected inflation relief. Accelerating bank credit to industry signals a revival in private capital expenditure, expanding order books for capital goods majors like Larsen & Toubro. Expected disinflation gives the Reserve Bank of India space to cut policy rates, lowering borrowing costs. Fortnightly RBI credit growth data will confirm whether capex demand sustains.
ET Economy · +1 other
Leak, conflict and loss of arbitration: inside a Tata Power Mumbai FIR
Tata Power filed a criminal complaint against an arbitrator and former employees following a Singapore tribunal's $490 million award to Kleros Capital. The ruling orders share seizures of two Tata Power subsidiaries. This dispute introduces severe balance sheet risk, requiring earnings provisions and pressuring Tata Power's valuation multiples. Court proceedings on the stay of share enforcement will determine immediate asset security.
Mint Companies
Saudi East-West oil pipeline hit in Medina region, state media reports
Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline sustained an attack in the Medina region, threatening oil supply lines. Energy infrastructure strikes push global crude prices higher, increasing India's import bill and pressuring the rupee. Higher crude squeezes gross margins for oil marketing companies like BPCL, while improving realisations for upstream producer ONGC. Saudi Aramco's repair timeline will clarify the extent of supply disruption.
Reuters Business
Gold, silver extend gains as softer oil prices ease inflation concerns
Spot gold surged past $4,100 per ounce while international crude oil prices softened on inflation relief. Lower crude reduces India's import bill, easing rupee pressure and supporting margins for paint and tire manufacturers. Higher bullion prices directly expand collateral values and loan books for gold-loan NBFCs such as Muthoot Finance.
BS Markets · +1 other
Companies and earnings
Food industry pushes back on WHO guidance for products with added colour, sweeteners
Global food manufacturers are actively lobbying against new World Health Organization guidelines that restrict artificial colors and non-sugar sweeteners. If the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India aligns local regulations with these WHO norms, packaged food companies like Nestlé India and Britannia face product reformulation expenses and margin pressure. Watch for upcoming FSSAI draft notifications on front-of-pack labeling for confirmation.
Reuters Business
Trump administration's embrace of "perp" futures sets off risk alarms for Wall Street stalwarts
The US administration is considering approvals for perpetual futures, which are derivative contracts without expiration dates historically confined to cryptocurrency trading. Major global exchanges warn that perpetual contracts increase systemic risk and market volatility by allowing excessive leverage. This development has no direct financial impact on Indian equities, as SEBI regulations strictly prohibit non-expiring derivative instruments in domestic capital markets.
ET Markets
BP sells 49.9% stake in Indonesian petrol station venture, partner firm says
BP selling its 49.9% stake in an Indonesian fuel retail joint venture has no material connection or financial impact on Indian equities.
Reuters Business
Chemplast Sanmar shares jump over 11% in biggest single-day gain in 10 months as Q2 rally gathers pace
Chemplast Sanmar reported Q2 revenue growth of 28% year-on-year to ₹1,323 crore, with EBITDA reaching ₹111 crore and net loss narrowing to ₹5 crore. Operational recovery was driven by higher specialty PVC sales volumes and expanding spreads over imported vinyl chloride monomer feedstock. Sustained PVC-VCM spreads in coming weeks will confirm whether the company returns to net profitability next quarter.
Mint Markets
Geopolitics
Trump admin hits indian solar panels with tariffs topping 100 percent - BizPac Review
The US administration imposed anti-dumping duties exceeding 100% on Indian solar cell and module exports. This trade action directly hits export revenues and dollar realizations for listed domestic manufacturers like Waaree Energies and Premier Energies. A formal response or legal challenge filed with the US Department of Commerce will determine if these punitive duty rates can be revised.
Geopolitics
Brent crude slides to $93 as petrol prices remain high - Daily Trust
Brent crude fell to $93 per barrel while domestic retail petrol prices stayed flat, expanding marketing margins for state-run oil refiners. Lower crude prices reduce raw material costs for paint companies, tire manufacturers, and airlines by easing input inflation. If Brent stays below $90, state marketing companies will likely face political pressure to pass on retail price cuts.
Crude and commodities
Oil prices plummeted as the US president signaled military restraint toward Iran. - Vietnam.vn
Crude oil futures dropped sharply after the US signaled military restraint toward Iran, unwinding the geopolitical risk premium priced into energy markets. This de-escalation eases pressure on India's current account deficit and helps stabilize the rupee against the US dollar. Stable currency expectations reduce downside risk for rate-sensitive bank stocks and import-heavy capital goods manufacturers.
